Subject: SIG questionnaire: scanner retention policy & false-positive handling

Hi Sofia / Kimberly,

We're working through the SIG questionnaire and have two follow-ups on your vulnerability management artifacts before we can mark the section complete:

1) Scanner retention: the SIG asks for retention windows for raw scanner outputs (full findings, stack traces, binary snippets). Can you confirm how long Redwood keeps raw scan blobs and whether customers can request immediate purging?

2) False-positive process: we need a short description of (a) suppression rules, (b) re-open conditions, and (c) who owns exception approval. Specifically, do you have a documented tuning/playbook and an API for customers to submit suspected false positives?

If you can send the specific retention policy document and a brief FP handling playbook (or links), that would be ideal. We have an internal SOC 2 evidence checkpoint tomorrow afternoon, so a quick turn would be appreciated.

Thanks — Emma

Emma —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, full artifacts attached and linked below.

- Raw scanner outputs retention: default 90 days for full finding exports (raw payloads and scanner metadata). Aggregated summary records (finding index, normalized CVE records) retained 2 years. Customers on Dedicated/Private can request custom retention (shorter or longer) via support ticket; immediate purging is supported for hosted customers but requires a ticket and a maximum SLA window of 72 hours for confirmation.

- False-positive process: we operate a three-tier FP workflow:
  * Automated suppression (heuristics + historical fingerprinting) for noisy signatures — automatic 7-day suppression window with auto-reopen on new evidence.
  * Manual triage by Vulnerability Ops (owner: Vulnerability Manager) for suspected FPs — ownership for exception approval lies with Vulnerability Ops/Customer Security Liaison; exceptions logged in Jira (see SEC-1198).
  * Customer API: yes — customers can mark a finding as suspected FP via the /v1/scan-findings/{id}/feedback endpoint; submissions create a triage ticket and a 48-hour acknowledgement SLA.

I've attached our scanner retention policy and the FP tuning playbook. Also sharing the internal Drive link to the living playbook for the SIG reviewers.

Attachments:
- redwood_scanner_retention_policy_v1.pdf (retention windows, purge workflow, encryption at rest)
- fp_tuning_playbook_v2.md (suppression rules, sample signatures, re-open criteria, manual triage checklist)

Drive: https://drive.google.com/redwood/pioneer-scanner-retention-v1
Jira reference: JIRA-SEC-1198

If you'd like, we can schedule a 20-minute walkthrough with Vulnerability Ops to run through the suppression examples.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Emma — adding a quick operational note on CVE remediation SLAs and evidence export.
